parsedVerdict.reasoning: All three files belong to the same concern: business rules and invariants of the order/stock domain. DomainError.ts holds one error hierarchy, and every error in the module comes from it. guards.ts covers the value-validation rules and throws only InvalidValueError from that hierarchy. StockAllocationService.ts handles reservation, release and commit across many lines. It hands per-product decisions to Product (canReserve, reserve, release, commit) instead of redoing the stock math itself, and it reports failures with the shared domain errors (InsufficientStockError, StockAccountingError). No rule is written in two places: the check that stock is sufficient stays in Product.canReserve, and the non-empty and non-negative-integer checks live only in guards.ts. No file works around the module's own abstractions.
